categories.name: People & Skills
categories.description: Assessment of workforce capabilities and skills development

questions.text: How well does the organizational design align with the strategic goals of HR operations?

options.text: Very low - No alignment with strategic goals
Low - Minimal alignment with strategic goals
Moderate - Some alignment with strategic goals
High - Good alignment with strategic goals
Very high - Full alignment with strategic goals and proactive design

questions.text: How flexible is the organizational design to adapt to changing needs?

options.text: Very limited - Rigid structure with no flexibility
Limited - Some flexibility but primarily role-based
Moderate - Mix of role-based and skills-based design
Good - Mostly skills-based with some role flexibility
Very good - Fully skills-based design with high adaptability

questions.text: How would the labour / talent availability across all existing GBS locations be described?

options.text: Very low - Severe talent shortages in all locations
Low - Limited talent availability in most locations
Moderate - Average talent availability across locations
High - Good talent availability in most locations
Very high - Abundant talent availability across all locations

questions.text: How well are employees trained on new processes?

options.text: Not at all - No training provided
Limited - Basic training provided
Moderate - Training provided but inconsistent
Good - Regular training sessions held
Excellent - Comprehensive training with continuous updates

questions.text: How well-documented are your organization's HR processes?

options.text: Not documented - No formal documentation exists
Poorly documented - Limited or outdated documentation
Partially documented - Some processes are documented
Mostly documented - Most processes have up-to-date documentation
Fully documented - All processes are thoroughly documented and regularly updated

questions.text: To what extent are your HR processes data-driven?

options.text: Not data-driven - Decisions based on intuition
Minimally data-driven - Basic reporting only
Partially data-driven - Some analytics used
Mostly data-driven - Regular use of analytics
Fully data-driven - Advanced analytics and predictive modeling

questions.text: How would you rate the consistency of this process across different geographical locations?

options.text: Very inconsistent - Significant variation across locations
Inconsistent - Some locations follow different processes
Moderately consistent - Most locations follow similar processes
Consistent - Minor variations, but overall process is similar
Highly consistent - Standardized process across all locations

questions.text: How effective are the controls in place for monitoring and managing the process?

options.text: Very ineffective - No controls or monitoring in place
Ineffective - Minimal controls, rarely monitored
Somewhat effective - Basic controls, inconsistently monitored
Effective - Controls in place and regularly monitored
Highly effective - Comprehensive controls with proactive monitoring and management

categories.name: AI Adoption
categories.description: Implementation of AI in HR functions

questions.text: To what extent has your organization adopted AI in HR functions?

options.text: No adoption - No AI tools used
Early exploration - Researching AI options
Initial adoption - Piloting AI in limited areas
Partial adoption - AI used in several HR functions
Full adoption - AI integrated across all HR functions

questions.text: How mature is your organization's AI governance framework?

options.text: Non-existent - No AI governance
Basic - Informal guidelines only
Developing - Formal policies being created
Established - Comprehensive framework in place
Advanced - Mature governance with continuous improvement

categories.name: Data Readiness
categories.description: Quality and accessibility of HR data

questions.text: How would you describe your organization's level of data standardization / Quality of data in HR operations?

options.text: Very poor - Data is inconsistent, unstandardized, and unreliable
Poor - Some data standards exist but significant quality issues remain
Average - Data is somewhat standardized with occasional quality issues
Good - Data is mostly standardized and of high quality
Excellent - Data is fully standardized, high quality, and trusted for decision-making

questions.text: To what extent is HR data transparent and accessible to relevant stakeholders in your organization?

options.text: Very low - Data is not accessible or transparent to stakeholders
Low - Limited access to data, transparency issues
Moderate - Some data is accessible, but transparency is inconsistent
High - Most data is accessible and transparent to stakeholders
Very high - All relevant data is fully accessible and transparent to stakeholders

questions.text: What level of advanced analytics and predictive insights does your HR data system offer?

options.text: Very low - No advanced analytics or predictive insights available
Low - Basic analytics only, no predictive capabilities
Moderate - Some advanced analytics, limited predictive insights
High - Advanced analytics with some predictive capabilities
Very high - Comprehensive advanced analytics and robust predictive insights available

questions.text: How efficient is your HR data processing and reporting?

options.text: Very inefficient - Data processing is slow and reporting is manual
Inefficient - Some automation, but significant manual effort required
Moderately efficient - Mostly automated with occasional manual tasks
Efficient - Highly automated data processing and reporting
Very efficient - Fully automated, real-time data processing and reporting with minimal manual intervention

questions.text: How mature is your organization's hybrid work model?

options.text: No hybrid model - Traditional office-only approach
Basic hybrid - Limited remote work options
Moderate hybrid - Flexible work arrangements available
Advanced hybrid - Optimized for both remote and office work
AI-optimized hybrid - Dynamic work arrangements based on analytics
